sentences.text: The present petition has been filed assailing the order dated 05.01.2023 passed by the respondent No.1/Collector whereby the application filed by the petitioners for return of the land has been rejected.
2. It is the case of the petitioners that their land has been acquired by the National Highway Authority of India in March, 2005.
The land remained unutilized for more than 15 years.

They have filed an application under Section 101 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (in short "the Act of 2013") before the Collector who was the competent authority under Section 3(G) of National Highways Authority of India for return of the land.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The aforesaid application has been rejected vide impugned order.

3. It is argued that the similar issue came before the Hon'ble Supreme Court for consideration in the case of Project Director National Highways Vs. M. Hakeem SLP (Civil) No.13020 of 2020 decided on 20.07.2021 wherein it was held that in the matter of welfare provision land owner cannot be discriminated on the basis of proceedings commenced and terminated on the basis of different enactment.

entities.text: Project Director National Highways Vs. M. Hakeem SLP (Civil) No.13020 of 2020
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The reason for rejection which is shown is that the provision of 101 of the Act of 2013 is applicable in only those cases wherein the land has been required under this Act.

It is argued that once the legal proposition has been settled by the Hon'ble Supreme Court coupled with the fact that the land acquired in March, 2005 has remained unutilized for more than 15 years then in all fairness the authority should have returned the land back to the petitioners.

4. Heard learned counsels for the parties and perused the record.
5.
The only question which has come up for consideration before this court is whether in terms of Section 101 of the Act, 2013, the land can be returned back to the petitioners.

Section 101 of the Act,
2013 reads as under :-
"101. Return of unutilised land -

When any land, acquired under this Act remains unutilised for a period of five years from the date of taking over the possession, the same shall be returned to the original owner or owners or their legal heirs, as the case may be, or to the Land Bank of the appropriate Government by reversion in the manner as may be prescribed by the appropriate Government.

sentences.text: Explanation -

For the purpose of this section, "Land Bank"
means a governmental entity that focuses on the conversion of Government owned vacant,
abandoned, unutilised acquired lands and tax-deliquent properties into productive use."

6 . From a perusal of the aforesaid section, it is clear that the provision of Section 101 of the Act,
2013 are applicable to the land which has been acquired under the Act of 2013.
7. Admittedly, the land of the petitioners was acquired way back in the year 2005 when this Act was not even in existence.
This Act has come into force with effect from 01.01.2014.
Under these circumstances, provision of Section 101 of the Act, 2013 is not applicable to the case of the petitioners.

8. As far as the argument that the issue is settled by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of M.
Hakeem (supra) is concerned, the aforesaid case deals with the question that "whether the power of the court under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 to set aside an award of an arbitrator would include the power to modify such an award."
The aforesaid question has been answered in the aforesaid case.

It has nothing to do with the implementation of Section 101 of the Act, 2013.
9 .
Counsel appearing for the petitioners could not point out any law in support of this argument.
The case law which has been relied upon is on different facts and circumstances and a different question of law was considered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court.
The same is not applicable in the present case.

Once, the language of the Act is clear and cogent and makes the provision under Section 101 of the Act, 2013 to be applicable to the land acquired under the Act of 2013, no relief can be extended to the petitioners.
10. The petition sans merit and is accordingly dismissed.
No order as to costs.
(RAVI MALIMATH)
